rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and produce telemetry. Geometry: five sensors spaced 2 cm apart across the line (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m) and 5 cm ahead of the axle, so the robot sees the line early enough to steer. Sensor size 12 mm is about half the 25 mm tape width, giving a clear, graded response. The 120 mm wheel track, 30 mm wheel radius, 120 mm body width and 0.8 kg mass are mid-range values that keep the off-track limit at 0.06 m and the yaw inertia moderate. Controller: weights are antisymmetric (-1.5 to +1.5), so the signal is signed and centred on zero. kp = 2.0 gives a turn of up to about 3 units (about 1000 PWM difference at full signal), which is firm enough to follow bends without a large integral term. ki = 0 avoids windup on the bends. kd = 0.05 adds mild damping against overshoot. base_speed = 1.6 (PWM fraction 0.8) is chosen to target roughly 1.5 m/s average while leaving room for steering. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: the robot completes the oval and s-bend with few line-loss events. I expect the slalom to be the hardest, with the most oscillation and the most risk of line loss. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp = 2 is near the oscillation limit, so steering_oscillation will rise if kd is too low; (2) base_speed 1.6 can reach the 3 s time limit; (3) the sensor spacing is adequate for the tightest bend. Next measurements: completion_time and progress to check speed; rms_error and max_error to check tracking; steering_oscillation to check damping; line_loss_events to check sensor coverage on the slalom.
